stories.title: Implement DID publishing and resolution via Mainline DHT
stories.description:
Implement publish_did_document and resolve_did per ADR-003 criteria 2-3.

`publish_did_document(identity)`: publish DID Document to Mainline DHT as BEP44 signed mutable item via pkarr. Monotonically increasing sequence number. Idempotent.

stories.title: Implement DID key rotation and identity migration
stories.description:
Implement ADR-003 criteria 4a-4c: the three-layer key rotation architecture.

**Layer 1 — rotate_active_key**: Generate new Active Signing Key. Update DID Document (new verification method, retire old as #retired-{seq}). Sign with Identity Key. Publish to DHT with incremented sequence. DID string does NOT change.

**Layer 2 — migrate_identity**: Create new DID using pre-rotation key. Link old → new DID via alsoKnownAs. Old Identity Key signs new. Publish both documents. Return DidRotationEvent.

**Layer 3 — verify_migration**: Verify cryptographic linkage (old key signed new key). Verify pre-rotation proof if present (SHA-256 commitment match). Return strong/moderate assurance level.

Define DidRotationEvent, MigrationProof, PreRotationProof structs per ADR-003.

stories.title: Implement MLS epoch ratcheting with EpochGraceStore and update proposals
stories.description:
Implement ADR-001 criteria 6-7.

**ratchet(group, commit)**: process Commit, advance to new epoch. Old epoch keys enter grace window. Grace window closes when: (a) all members sent in new epoch, or (b) 30 seconds (hard ceiling). After grace closes, old keys destroyed — forward secrecy. Messages arriving after grace are unrecoverable → emit StaleEpochMessage event.

**EpochGraceStore** (epoch_grace.rs): in-memory only, indexed by epoch number, auto-purged by timer. NOT accessible to any code path other than decrypt with matching epoch. Uses tokio::time::sleep for 30s ceiling.

**update(group)**: issue MLS Update proposal — fresh HPKE keypair, ratchet sender's tree path. Post-compromise security. Returns (UpdateProposal, Commit).

stories.title: Implement UCAN validation pipeline and NonceTracker
stories.description:
Implement ADR-009 criteria 4, 7: the 8-check validation pipeline and nonce tracking.

validate_ucan(context_handle, token, required_capability) -> Result<(), UcanError>: 8 checks in order:
1. Verify UCAN signature chain (each delegation signature valid)
2. Verify root issuer is context creator
3. Verify audience matches presenting agent's DID
4. Verify token grants the required capability
5. Verify capability is within context's ceiling
6. Verify nonce not seen before (NonceTracker) + add to seen set
7. Verify token not revoked (check revocation list)
8. Verify token not expired

Each check returns a specific UcanError variant on failure.

NonceTracker struct: HashMap<String, (u64, u64)> — nonce -> (first_seen_timestamp, token_expiry_timestamp). Context-scoped.
- Nonce format validation: Parse timestamp prefix, validate random suffix is 32 hex chars.
- Freshness check: Timestamp prefix within now +/- 5 minutes (clock skew tolerance per §9.14).
- check_and_record(nonce, token_expiry) -> Result<(), UcanError>: Validate format, validate freshness, reject if seen, record if new.
- Replay window: Retain nonce until max(token_expiry + 5 min, first_seen + 24 hours).
- prune(): Remove expired entries. Runs every 1000 check_and_record calls or every 10 minutes.
- Persisted to scp-platform Storage for crash recovery.

Note: ADR-009 criterion 4 recommends building the full 11-check validation pipeline from ADR-016 directly (ADR-016 is a strict superset adding chain verification, attenuation checking, and structured nonce validation). The 8 checks above map to ADR-016 steps 1-2, 4-6, 8-11. The implementation SHOULD target the 11-check pipeline to avoid rework in Phase 3.

stories.title: Phase 2 end-to-end integration test
stories.description:
The ultimate Phase 2 acceptance criterion — a single test exercising all 5 ADRs together with Phase 1's crypto stack. Follows the 12-step integration scenario from the ADR document:

1. Alice creates identity (Phase 1 ADR-003) and context with ceiling [messaging, tool_invoke], roles [admin, member], one "calculator" tool, TTL 5 minutes, memory scope ephemeral (ADR-008)
2. Context assigned to 3 relays via TransportManager (ADR-012)
3. Bob creates identity, discovers context, and joins (ADR-008)
4. Bob assigned "member" role with UCAN tokens for messages:read, messages:write, tool_invoke_all (ADR-009)
5. Alice sends message. UCAN validated. Envelope created, multi-relay published (ADR-012). Event logged in Merkle tree (ADR-011)

9. Both generate consistency checkpoints (ADR-011). Merkle roots match
10. TTL expires. Context transitions to Expired (ADR-008). MLS + sender keys destroyed. Relay deletion requests sent
11. Event log Merkle tree survives — hashes/proofs persist even though content is unreadable
12. Throughout: relay reliability tracked, relay sets partitioned

stories.title: Bootstrap Python SDK package structure and foundation modules
stories.description: Establish the pure Python scp_sdk package that wraps the _scp_core PyO3 extension module. This story creates the package scaffold, build configuration, synchronous execution infrastructure, and the exception hierarchy. The sync.py module must provide a run_sync() helper backed by a dedicated background event loop running on a daemon thread, accessed thread-safely via asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe. The background loop is created lazily on the first call to run_sync() via _get_sync_loop(), which uses double-checked locking with a threading.Lock to ensure thread safety. This design is safe to call from any context, including from within an already-running event loop, because it routes work to a separate background loop rather than nesting event loops. The errors.py module must define the full exception hierarchy rooted at ScpError so all downstream modules can import from it. The pyproject.toml must use maturin as the build backend, declare Python 3.10+ as the minimum, and include optional dependency groups for langchain and mcp integrations.

stories.title: Implement MCP server core: tool listing with UCAN filtering and tool invocation routing
stories.description:
Implement the MCP server core logic in `server.rs`. No transport I/O here — pure request/response dispatch that transports will call.

`McpServer` struct holds: agent DID, SCP client handle (from ADR-013 bridge), list of joined context IDs. Implement:

**Tool listing** (`handle_tools_list`): For each joined context, query the agent's UCAN capabilities. Include only tools the agent has `MessagesRead` or context-specific capability for. Prepend context_id as namespace: `"{context_id}/{tool_name}"`. Always include the three built-in tools for each context if the agent is a member. Return `ToolsListResult` with full `ToolDefinition` per tool (name=namespaced, description, inputSchema as JSON Schema object). JSON Schema for `send_message`: `{type: object, properties: {content: {type: string}, message_type: {type: string, enum: ["text", "binary"]}}, required: ["content"]}`. For `read_messages`: `{type: object, properties: {limit: {type: integer, minimum: 1, maximum: 100}, since_sequence: {type: integer}}}`. For `list_members`: `{type: object, properties: {}}`.

**Tool invocation** (`handle_tools_call`): Parse `ContextNamespacedTool` from tool name. Validate UCAN capability for the agent in the named context. Validate tool input against the tool's input schema (JSON Schema validation) — reject with -32602 (invalid params) if input does not conform. If built-in: dispatch to built-in handler (send_message calls SCP send, read_messages fetches from store, list_members queries context membership). If registered tool: route through SCP context tool invocation. Validate tool output against the tool's output schema (JSON Schema validation) — log warning on mismatch but do not reject (output validation is informational). Attach provenance to result: wrap `ToolsCallResult` content with provenance record using field names `source` (with `mcp:` prefix, e.g. `"mcp:send_message"`), `invoked_by` (agent DID string), `context` (context_id), `timestamp` (unix_timestamp_ms), `server_info`. Return JSON-RPC error on failure using appropriate error codes.

stories.title: Implement MCP server stdio transport with MCP lifecycle handling
stories.description:
Implement the stdio transport for the MCP server in `stdio.rs`. This is the primary integration path for MCP hosts (Claude Desktop, etc.) that spawn `scp-mcp serve` as a subprocess.

**Transport protocol**: Line-delimited JSON over stdin/stdout. Each message is one JSON object per line (`\n`-terminated). stderr is for diagnostics only — never write JSON-RPC messages to stderr.

**`StdioTransport` struct**: Wraps `McpServer`. Exposes `async fn run(&self) -> Result<(), McpError>` that loops: read line from stdin → deserialize as `JsonRpcRequest<Value>` → dispatch through `McpServer::dispatch` → serialize response → write to stdout → flush.

**MCP lifecycle**: Handle `initialize` method specially before routing to server dispatch. On `initialize`: store `clientInfo` from params, return `InitializeResult` with `protocolVersion: "2024-11-05"`, `capabilities: {tools: {listChanged: true}, resources: {subscribe: true}}`, `serverInfo: {name: "scp-mcp", version: env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")}`. Handle `notifications/initialized` (client notification after initialize, no response required). Handle `ping` → respond with empty `{}` result.

**Server-initiated notifications**: Maintain a list of active stdio client writers. When the tool list changes (triggered by `McpServer` tool-change events), write `notifications/tools/list_changed` JSON-RPC notification to stdout. This ensures stdio clients receive dynamic tool update notifications per ADR AC-7, which requires ALL MCP clients (stdio AND SSE) receive these notifications.

**Error handling**: Malformed JSON line → send JSON-RPC parse error response (-32700) and continue loop. EOF on stdin → clean shutdown. Any individual dispatch error must NOT kill the loop — log to stderr and continue.

**Shutdown**: When `stdin` closes (EOF), call a shutdown hook (no-op for now, reserved) and return `Ok(())`.

Update `Cargo.toml` to add `tokio` with `io-util` feature if not present. The `run` loop must use `tokio::io::AsyncBufReadExt` for async stdin reading.

stories.title: Implement MCP server SSE transport, resource listing, and dynamic tool updates
stories.description:
Implement the SSE transport and resource listing for the MCP server in `sse.rs` using axum.

**SSE transport**: HTTP server with two endpoints: `GET /sse` for server-to-client SSE stream (Content-Type: text/event-stream), `POST /message` for client-to-server JSON-RPC requests. SSE messages use `data:` lines with JSON-RPC objects, terminated by `\n\n`. Client connects to `/sse`, receives SSE stream. Client sends JSON-RPC requests via POST to `/message`, receives JSON-RPC response in HTTP response body (200 OK, application/json). `SseTransport` struct: `bind_addr: SocketAddr`, wraps `Arc<McpServer>`. Expose `async fn serve(&self) -> Result<(), McpError>`.

**MCP lifecycle over SSE**: On `GET /sse` connection, immediately send a `endpoint` event: `event: endpoint\ndata: /message\n\n`. Then hold connection open for server-initiated notifications.

**SSE connection lifecycle (AC-5)**: Implement keep-alive mechanism: send SSE comment lines (`:keep-alive\n\n`) at a configurable interval (default 30 seconds) to prevent proxy/client timeouts. Handle client reconnection: accept `Last-Event-ID` header on `GET /sse` reconnect requests and replay any missed notifications since that event ID. Assign monotonically increasing event IDs to all server-initiated notifications (`id:` field in SSE events).

**Resource listing** (add to `McpServer` in `server.rs`): Handle `resources/list` method — return `ResourcesListResult` with resources for all joined contexts. Resource URIs: `scp://{context_id}/events` (mimeType: application/json, name: "{context_id} events"), `scp://{context_id}/members` (mimeType: application/json), `scp://{context_id}/tools` (mimeType: application/json). Handle `resources/read` method — parse URI, fetch data from SCP store (events: last 50 messages as JSON array; members: current member list; tools: registered tool list), return `ResourcesReadResult` with `TextResourceContents` (uri, mimeType, text as JSON string).

**Resource subscriptions**: Handle `resources/subscribe` — map subscription to SCP event stream for that context_id. When new events arrive, push `notifications/resources/updated` notification over SSE stream to subscribed clients.

**Dynamic tool updates**: When a context's tool list changes (new tool registered or deregistered), push `notifications/tools/list_changed` notification over all active SSE connections.

stories.title: Implement MCP client with SCP provenance wrapping for external MCP servers
stories.description:
Implement the MCP client in `client.rs` that connects to external MCP servers and wraps tool invocations with SCP provenance.

`McpClientConfig` enum: `Stdio { command: String, args: Vec<String> }`, `Sse { base_url: String }`. `McpClient` struct: holds config, connected transport handle, and discovered server capabilities. Does NOT store agent DID or context ID — these are per-invocation concerns per ADR-015 AC-6.

**`connect(config: McpClientConfig) -> Result<McpClient, McpError>`**: Takes only config (no agent_did or context_id). For Stdio: spawn subprocess with `tokio::process::Command` (use `tokio` with `process` feature), connect stdin/stdout pipes, send `initialize` request and await `InitializeResult`. For SSE: HTTP connect to `{base_url}/sse` using `hyper`, read `endpoint` event to discover POST endpoint URL, send `initialize` request via POST. Store discovered server capabilities.

**`list_tools(&self) -> Result<Vec<ToolDefinition>, McpError>`**: Send `tools/list` JSON-RPC request, return parsed `ToolsListResult.tools`. This is an async method.

**`invoke(&self, tool: &str, input: Value, agent_did: &DID, context_id: &ContextId) -> Result<ToolsCallResult, McpError>`**: Takes tool, input, plus per-invocation agent_did and context_id for SCP provenance (matching ADR AC-6 Python API: `invoke(tool=..., input=..., context=..., identity=...)`). Send `tools/call` JSON-RPC request with given name and input. On success: wrap result with SCP provenance metadata — add to result content a provenance record: `{"type": "scp_provenance", "source": "mcp:{tool}", "invoked_by": agent_did.to_string(), "context": context_id.to_string(), "timestamp": unix_timestamp_ms, "server_info": self.server_info}`. Return `ToolsCallResult` with provenance prepended to content vec.

**ID management**: Generate sequential JSON-RPC request IDs (`u64`, starting at 1, atomic increment). Correlate responses by ID.

stories.title: Implement UCAN types, capability URI parsing, and JWT structure
stories.description:
Define the core UCAN data model and capability URI system. mod.rs exposes UcanToken, UcanHeader, UcanPayload, and Attenuation structs with full serde support. UcanToken.signature is Ed25519Signature (not raw bytes). capability.rs implements URI parsing for the scp:ctx:{context_id}/{capability} scheme, capability matching with wildcard support (scp:ctx:*/{cap} and scp:ctx:{id}/*), and ceiling intersection (compute the narrowest capability set from two attenuation arrays). JWT-format UCAN parsing must base64url-decode the header and payload components, validate structural fields (alg: EdDSA, typ: JWT, ucv: 0.10.0), and return a typed UcanToken on success. All parsing errors return UcanError::ParseError with a descriptive message.

This story also defines the NonceTracker and RevocationList struct types (without method implementations) in nonce.rs and revoke.rs respectively, so that SCP-040 and SCP-041 can reference them without a circular dependency. SCP-041 provides the method implementations on these types.

Note: This story builds on Phase 1 crypto primitives. Phase 2 Rust crates must also be complete before this work begins.

stories.title: Implement UCAN minting and delegation
stories.description: Implement mint.rs with two functions. mint_ucan() creates a new root UCAN: generate a cryptographically random nonce in {unix_millis}-{32 hex characters (16 random bytes)} format, construct the att array scoped to the given context_id, populate all UcanPayload fields, sign the base64url(header).base64url(payload) string with the issuer's Ed25519 signing key, and return a signed UcanToken. expiry is required (not Option). delegate_ucan() creates a delegated UCAN: the first parameter is parent_token, followed by delegator, delegatee (audience DID of the new token), and attenuated_capabilities. Verify the delegator's DID matches the parent token's aud field (IssuerMismatch otherwise), verify each capability in attenuated_capabilities is a subset of the parent att via capability_match (CeilingViolation otherwise), set prf to include the parent token's CID, and sign with the delegator's Ed25519 key. delegate_ucan does not take an exp parameter (ADR does not specify delegation expiry behavior). stories.title: Implement 11-step UCAN validation pipeline
stories.description: Implement validate.rs with the complete validate_ucan() pipeline. The function signature is validate_ucan(context: &ValidateContext, token: &str, required_capability: &str) -> Result<(), UcanError> — it returns () on success, acting as a validation gate not a parser. ValidateContext holds: expected_aud DID, root_issuer DID (context creator), ceiling Attenuation list, nonce_tracker reference, revocation_list reference. The NonceTracker and RevocationList types used here are defined in SCP-038 (nonce.rs and revoke.rs); this story only implements the validation pipeline that consumes them. The 11 steps execute in order and fail fast on first error: (1) parse JWT via parse_ucan_jwt, (2) verify Ed25519 signature over base64url(header).base64url(payload) using iss public key derived from DID, (3) chain verification — for each CID in prf, fetch parent token and recursively validate; parent aud must equal child iss (ChainError otherwise), (4) verify root token iss == context root_issuer, (5) verify token aud matches expected_aud, (6) capability match — required_capability present in att, (7) attenuation — each att entry is subset of parent att (CeilingViolation if delegated token is wider than parent), (8) ceiling check — no att entry exceeds ceiling, (9) nonce validation via nonce_tracker, (10) revocation check via revocation_list (RevocationError if token CID is revoked), (11) expiry — exp > now and nbf <= now.
